criteria.justification: The response explicitly states that the uncommon nature of the charged path 'doesn’t make it acceptable to surprise the customers who hit it' and refuses to ship based on the assumption that most will use the free path.

The response suggests disclosing the charge 'properly wherever customers need to see it', but fails to explicitly consider the risk of a blanket warning that might misrepresent the common, free-path case.

The candidate treats the disclosure gap as automatically decisive by immediately declaring it a 'launch blocker', rather than explicitly weighing the cost of delaying the finalized launch against the gap.
The response avoids a strict binary choice by suggesting a narrowly scoped alternative: 'Disable or defer the paid-service path if that can be done safely' while launching the rest of the feature.
The candidate provides a specific, actionable plan to immediately gather key stakeholders (Legal, engineering, docs) to execute one of two concrete options, including end-to-end verification.
